question: Which group of monuments consists of the Vitthala Temple?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Group of Monuments at Hampi**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vitthala Temple** is part of the **Group of Monuments at Hampi**.
 
• Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka, is renowned for its rich history and impressive ruins of temples, palaces, and market streets from the Vijayanagara Empire, with the Vitthala Temple being one of its most iconic structures, famous for its intricate carvings and stone chariot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram**:

 
 
• Located in Tamil Nadu, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is famous for its rock-cut temples and intricately carved sculptures dating back to the Pallava dynasty.
 
• Notable monuments include the Shore Temple and the Pancha Rathas, showcasing exceptional Dravidian architecture.
 
 
 
• **Group of Monuments at Pattadakal**:
 
 
• Situated in Karnataka, this UNESCO World Heritage Site features a mix of Hindu and Jain temples built during the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• It is known for its architectural brilliance, including the famous Virupaksha Temple and its contributions to early South Indian temple design.
 
 
 
• **Khajuraho Group of Monuments**:
 
 
• Located in Madhya Pradesh, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is renowned for its stunning temples adorned with intricate erotic sculptures and carvings.
 
• Built between 950 and 1050 AD by the Chandela dynasty, the temples are a significant example of Indian medieval architecture and art.
